statement: Three balances are level. On the first, 1 cube balances 3 balls. On the second, 2 balls balance 1 cone and 1 marble. On the third, 1 cone balances 3 marbles. All cubes weigh the same, and so do all balls, all cones and all marbles. How many marbles balance one cube?

choices.misconception: I found the weight of a ball, 2 marbles, instead of the weight of a cube.
I worked out what the 2 balls on the second balance weigh, 4 marbles, and took that as the weight of the cube.
I left out the marble on the second balance, so 2 balls balanced only a cone, 3 marbles, and a ball came out as 1.5 marbles.
I read the second balance as 1 ball balancing a cone and a marble, so a ball was 4 marbles and a cube 12.

hints: Start from the balance that uses only one kind of unknown object.
The third balance tells you a cone in marbles. Put that into the second balance to find a ball, then use the first balance to find a cube.
On the second balance, the cone and the marble together weigh 3 + 1 = 4 marbles, and that is the weight of 2 balls.

solutions.reliable: A cone weighs 3 marbles, so the right side of the second balance weighs 3 + 1 = 4 marbles. That is the weight of 2 balls, so one ball weighs 2 marbles. A cube balances 3 balls, which is 3 × 2 = 6 marbles. Check: 3 balls weigh 6 marbles, and 2 balls weigh 4 marbles, the same as a cone and a marble. The transferable idea: in a chain of balances, start with the one that has a single unknown and swap objects for marbles one step at a time.
solutions.elegant: Turn everything into marbles from the bottom of the chain up: cone = 3, so 2 balls = 3 + 1 = 4, so ball = 2, so cube = 3 × 2 = 6.

whyOnTest: Balance puzzles test substitution: swapping each object for what it balances, one balance at a time, until everything is in the same unit.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
